The performance-specific fact is that ISSUE bills September 12 as No-Neck Blues Band's first performance in thirteen years and explicitly says it will happen for one night only. Would A+ still capture the recommendation? No: for the US corridor there is a single announced chance, after a thirteen-year absence, to hear the collective return to approximately one hour of non-idiomatic group improvisation. Missing that exact return would create genuine regret for this Listening Notes thread, so protecting the night is warranted. S+ is not warranted because ISSUE describes a return rather than a farewell or final performance, and the presenter says the group is presently working on its thirty-sixth album; another future performance is therefore possible even though none is announced here.

events.factual_description: ISSUE Project Room presents No-Neck Blues Band at First Unitarian Congregational Society in Brooklyn on Saturday, September 12, 2026 at 8:00 PM. ISSUE states that the group will perform for the first time in thirteen years, for one night only, and describes the set as an approximately one-hour non-idiomatic collective improvisation. The event opens ISSUE's fall season during the 20th-anniversary year of its Artists-In-Residence program. ISSUE identifies No-Neck Blues Band as an improvising collective formed in New York City in 1993, notes founding member Keith Connolly's connection as a 2016 ISSUE Artist-In-Residence, and says the group is presently at work on what will be its thirty-sixth album. The authorized TicketSpice page lists general admission at $25 face value plus a $1 fee and verifies the venue address as 119 Pierrepont St, Brooklyn, NY 11201.

en.why_it_matters: Thirteen years without a No-Neck Blues Band performance turns this into more than another experimental booking. The collective is returning for one night to the open-form group improvisation that made its New York presence so distinctive, in a room presented by ISSUE during the anniversary season of its artist-residency program. The long silence and the one-night frame make the performance itself the reason to be there.
en.trip_verdict: From the DMV, I would protect Saturday night and make the dedicated New York trip if this experimental-improvisation thread matters. There is no nearby substitute date announced, and the thirteen-year gap makes waiting for a more convenient return a real gamble.
en.listen_before: No-Neck Blues Band — Sticks and Stones May Break My Bones But Names Will Never Hurt Me.

es.why_it_matters: Trece años sin una actuación de No-Neck Blues Band convierten esta fecha en algo muy distinto de otra noche de música experimental. El colectivo vuelve por una sola noche a esa improvisación grupal abierta que marcó su presencia en Nueva York, presentado por ISSUE en la temporada de aniversario de su programa de residencias. La pausa larga y el carácter único de la fecha hacen que la función misma sea la razón para estar ahí.
es.trip_verdict: Desde el DMV protegería la noche del sábado y sí haría el viaje dedicado a Nueva York si este hilo de improvisación experimental pesa en la escucha. No hay una fecha cercana que sirva de reemplazo y, después de trece años de silencio en vivo, apostar a que pronto habrá otra oportunidad sería arriesgado.
